forces.title: Strong Consumer Demand and Rising Incomes Drive Retailer Expansion
forces.description: India's large and young population, growing middle class, urbanization, and rising disposable incomes significantly bolster domestic consumption. This robust consumer base, combined with increased purchasing power and easy credit availability, fuels retailer confidence and expansion plans. As a result, retailers are opening new stores and expanding existing footprints, directly increasing demand for retail and mixed-use development spaces across major cities and even into Tier-II/III markets.

forces.title: Institutional Investment Growth in Commercial and Mixed-Use Developments
forces.description: Institutional investments in India's real estate sector are strong, with commercial (including retail) and mixed-use developments attracting significant capital inflows. In Q1 2026, commercial real estate accounted for 94% of total institutional investment. Specific transactions, such as the Rs. 681 crore investment in Nexus Select Trust (a retail REIT), highlight continued interest in REITs and platform-led models. This influx of capital provides developers with enhanced funding access for new projects and expansion.

forces.title: Shift to Experience-Driven Retail Reshapes Physical Store Requirements
forces.description: Consumer preferences are evolving, with a growing demand for experience-driven retail over traditional transactional shopping. Retailers are adapting by adopting experiential flagship stores, pop-up kiosks, and Gen Z-focused store formats. This necessitates a redesign of retail spaces, requiring developers to provide flexible, technologically advanced, and engaging environments within shopping malls and mixed-use projects. This structural shift drives demand for premium, adaptable, and well-designed retail real estate assets.

forces.title: Global Brands and Retailers Expand Physical Presence in India
forces.description: India continues to attract significant interest from international and domestic retailers due to its high growth potential. Brands like IKEA are making substantial investments to open new stores (25 new small/medium format stores), while others like Tim Hortons and Zudio are rapidly expanding their footprints. This consistent entry and expansion of global and national brands, including D2C players opening physical stores, directly translates into increased demand for new retail and mixed-use development projects and leasing activity.

forces.title: Strategic Mall Developments by Major Groups Create New Retail Hubs
forces.description: The revival of significant mall projects, such as the LuLu Group's Visakhapatnam mall, signals strong developer confidence and creates new opportunities for retail and mixed-use development. These large-scale projects, often developed in partnership with state governments, bring substantial investment and job creation. Such developments expand the availability of modern retail spaces, attract anchor tenants, and enhance the overall retail infrastructure, positioning specific regions as new retail hubs and driving further investment in the sector.

viewpoints.title: Retail leasing activity and new development for quality retail spaces shows strong growth
viewpoints.description: India's retail sector leasing surged past 4 million square feet in Q4 2025, reaching 8.9 million square feet for the full year across major cities like Hyderabad, Delhi-NCR, and Chennai. This robust demand is driven by a rising supply of quality retail spaces and new store openings. The market is also poised to add nearly 41 million square feet of new retail developments by 2028, supported by increasing consumer spending and the expansion of organized retail, indicating a positive outlook for retail real estate development.

viewpoints.title: Experience-driven retail is reshaping demand for physical store formats and leasing
viewpoints.description: A CBRE report highlights a significant shift in consumer preferences towards experience-driven retail, prompting retailers to adopt experiential flagship stores, pop-up kiosks, and Gen Z-focused formats. This trend is materially impacting retail leasing, which reached a record ~8.9 million sq. ft. in 2025. Developers of retail and mixed-use spaces must adapt by creating more dynamic and engaging environments to meet evolving retailer demands and attract affluent consumers, ensuring continued demand for premium retail destinations.

demand_drivers.driver: Rising supply of quality retail spaces
demand_drivers.description: The availability of high-quality retail infrastructure in major cities attracts new store openings and expansion by retailers.

demand_drivers.driver: New store openings and D2C brand expansion
demand_drivers.description: Retailers, including D2C brands, are increasingly expanding their physical presence in fashion, apparel, jewellery, cosmetics, and wellness categories, contributing significantly to leasing volume.

market_sizing.methodology: Total retail sector leasing activity across major cities in 2025.

demand_drivers.description: Increased disposable incomes and aspirational consumer classes drive demand for retail products and, consequently, retail space.
The growth and formalization of the retail sector lead to greater demand for professionally developed and managed retail properties.

demand_drivers.driver: Increasing demand for premium retail destinations
demand_drivers.description: Consumers seek higher quality shopping experiences, pushing developers to create modern and attractive retail environments.

market_sizing.methodology: Projected addition of new retail developments in India by 2028.

demand_drivers.driver: Continued interest in REITs and platform-led models
